question: The river Ganga divides the state of Bihar into ______ parts.
solution:
The correct answer is __**two**__.

__
 
• **The river Ganga divides the state of Bihar into two parts**__. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

 
• **Ganga **enters the boundary of Bihar at Chausa a village near Buxar after its confluence with Karmanasa.
 
• The Bihar plain is divided into** two unequal halves** by the river Ganga which flows through the middle from west to east.
 
• The most common soil in Bihar is Gangetic alluvium of the Indo-Gangetic plain region
 
• **Ganga river originates as Bhagirathi from the Gangotri glacier**.
 
 
• Alaknanda river joins Bhagirathi at Devprayag, onwards known as Ganga.
 
• It is joined by the river Yamuna at Allahabad.
 
• At Farraka, it bifurcates into Bhagirathi-Hugli in West Bengal and Padma - Meghna in Bangladesh.
 
• It drains into the Bay of Bengal.
 
• Tributaries- Yamuna, Gandak, Ramganga, Son, Ghaghra, Gomti, Kosi, Tamsa, Punpun, and Mahananda.
